So what specifically is said will happen under ABS? First we need to understand the concept of goods order. A first order good is one that provides directly one of your needs. A hot meal in front of you is a first order good. A second order good is something that someone values because it indirectly helps them provide for their first order needs.

Next we need to understand how demand for one order of good converts to a second order good. Let's say we are in the business of providing comedy videos. What people value is a duplication of a video file that they can watch. The second order of that good is the fact that the film has been produced and that we have a file we can copy from. Now the whole market of comedy videos has a certain level of demand (volume). We are simplifying by picking a product who's first order good has zero variable cost. By producing a video we expect to capture a certain amount of that market which will pay us a dividend in periods. The net pressent value of which is the total cost we would be willing to incure to produce our film. This covers costs of third order goods that we use to help produce the film. That net present value formula takes into account interest rates. When interest rate are lower we are willing to spend more to produce the film. Let's say we delegated that to someone else. How much would we be willing to pay. Net present values can be much larger than the amount of an annual period.
